grammar_only: The specimens were cooled from 130 °C to 20 °C at 4 °C/min, and their mass was recorded before immersion. Each specimen was then immersed in toluene for 24 h; the resulting mass changes do not, by themselves, establish network degradation.
paragraph_revision: Across five separately prepared devices measured at 22 °C, surface treatment increased the mean sensitivity from 0.8 to 1.3 kPa−1 over the pressure range 0–2 kPa, although the statistical significance of this increase was not tested. Optical imaging showed a larger contact area under load after treatment, with no resolvable change in film thickness. The larger contact area may contribute to the increased sensitivity, but it cannot be established as the sole cause because the mechanical modulus was not measured and changes in bulk stiffness cannot be ruled out. A matched-modulus control would help distinguish these explanations. The sensor retained 94% of its initial response after 200 loading cycles at 1 kPa; this result does not establish long-term durability beyond the tested conditions.
preserve_voice: The interface, rather than the bulk film, set the limit on adhesion. We reached this conclusion by changing the surface treatment while keeping the film formulation and cure unchanged. Untreated specimens separated at the interface; treated specimens failed within the film. The result does not identify the bonding mechanism, but it locates the weakest link under the conditions tested. For this system, that distinction is enough to guide the next experiment.
